basis.text: Fremantle's diary of 2 July 1863 (Hood with Lee, Hill and Longstreet on the ridge at 5 a.m.) and Shepherd's report of 27 July 1863 (Official Records 27/2 p. 420: the Second Georgia of Hood's division resumed the march at 3 a.m. and halted after some 3 miles), read with Hood's letter of 1875, Polley and Freeman's computation for the head of the column.

default.label: About 05:00 (sunrise to 05:30): Hood and the head of his division on the ridge; the tail could be up by 07:30

animation.note: 05:00 is the earliest time a writer of the day places Hood on the ridge (Fremantle's diary); the memoir value (sunrise, about 04:35) stays selectable and is not the floor; the soldiers come in as a march along the road from Marsh Creek, the tail by about 07:30 (C-005-P3)

default.note: The head is shown at 05:00; Freeman computes the whole division up by about 07:30 (P3) and Longstreet's letter of 1875 and Meade's narrative close up both divisions about 08:00 (P6). Law's brigade was not with the column; it rejoined about noon.

support.quote: As the sun rose at Gettysburg on July 2 at 4:32, it probably is approximately correct to say that Longstreet joined Lee on Seminary Ridge at 5:15 or about that time [...] is less important than that of the appearance of his men. support.note: Report of 27 July 1863, Official Records Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 2 p. 420 (report no. 459). The first text layer prints ".3 a. m." and "13 p. m."; a second, independent scan and OCR (OR27-2-SCAN2-C005) prints "At 3 a. m." and "12 p. m." (midnight). The page image could not be fetched. inference.step: Freeman takes the 3 a.m. start of Hood's march (Shepherd's report, Official Records 27/2 p. 420) and an assumed five miles of road and says the head of the column 'should have been at the ridge by 5:30 a.m.'; the report itself gives about three miles, so 5:30 is a late bound for the head, not a sighting

reason_not_chosen.text: Freeman's 'by 5:30' is an upper bound computed from five miles of road; the regiment's report gives about three. It lies at the edge of the half-hour margin of the default.

inference.step: Fremantle's diary has Hood with Lee, Hill and Longstreet on the ridge when he arrived at 5 a.m.; Hood says his division began filing into the field soon after his own arrival. The division was about four miles out at midnight (Longstreet's report); the Second Georgia left its bivouac at 3 a.m. and halted after some 3 miles, that is about a mile from the town, where Law found the brigades resting; at Law's pace for the same day (24 miles in under nine hours) three miles take about 70 minutes and at a slow night pace two hours, so the head could be up from about 04:10; Freeman's 'by 5:30' and Polley's 'not later than an hour after sunrise' (about 05:35) close the late end. 05:00 is the one clock reading of the day that places Hood, and so the head that followed him, on the ridge; earlier times stay selectable.

witness.name: George Meade
witness.role: Captain and aide-de-camp to General Meade, author of the narrative published in 1913 (not on the Confederate side)

reason_not_chosen.text: Written 12 and 50 years later. Longstreet's own accounts disagree (8 a.m. in 1875, sunrise in 1896) and the diary of the day has him with Lee at 5 a.m.; it dates the closing up of both divisions.

weighing.summary: The sources agree on an early head and differ by what they measure. A diary of the day has Hood with Lee, Hill and Longstreet on the ridge at 5 a.m.; a regiment of his division reports leaving its bivouac at 3 a.m. and halting after some 3 miles; Hood, Longstreet and a Texas soldier later put the head at or soon after sunrise; Freeman computes it by 5:30. The later values (06:30, 07:30, 08:00) date the middle, the tail or the closing up of the column, and no source states 06:30. No source gives a clock for the division's own arrival, so the default is inferred.
weighing.who: Fremantle (British observer on Longstreet's staff) and Shepherd (Second Georgia, Hood's division) wrote what they saw or did. Hood and Longstreet were the generals present but wrote 12 and 33 years later; Polley, a Texas soldier, 47 years later; Freeman (1935) computed and Meade's narrative (1913) compiled. Kershaw's report (1 October 1863) concerns McLaws's division: 'did not leave camp until about sunrise'.
weighing.when: Fremantle's entry is of the day (rank 5); Shepherd's report is of 27 July 1863, 25 days after (rank 5). Hood's letter is of 28 June 1875, Longstreet's letter of 20 April 1875 and his book of 1896, Polley 1910, Meade 1913, Freeman 1935: reminiscence and later history (rank 2 and 1). The contemporaneous pair outranks the rest and is not contradicted by it.
weighing.where: Fremantle sat in a tree above Lee's group on the ridge; Shepherd marched in the column; Hood and Longstreet were on the ridge, and Freeman says Hood and McLaws 'rode ahead of their troops'; Law reached the field only shortly before noon and found Hood's other brigades resting about a mile from the town on the Chambersburg road; Freeman, Taylor and Meade were not there.
weighing.how_knew: Fremantle and Shepherd wrote what they saw and did. Hood wrote 'from memory'. Longstreet's accounts differ (8 a.m. in 1875, sunrise in 1896). Freeman computes: a 3 a.m. start and an assumed five miles. Law, of the same division on the same day, gives the pace: 24 miles from 3 a.m. to shortly before noon.
weighing.clock: Shepherd, Hood, Longstreet and Polley use the Confederate clock; Fremantle's watch is unspecified. The 20-minute difference between the two armies' clocks is not applied: it is smaller than the half-hour margin of the default. Sunrise on 2 July is 04:35 local mean time (the plan).
weighing.independence: Groups: fremantle; shepherd; hood-letter-1875 (Longstreet printed it in 1877 and again in 1896, so his 'sunrise' may rest on it); longstreet-1896; freeman (computes from Shepherd's 3 a.m.); polley; law. Fremantle and Shepherd are independent of each other and of the memoirs; the default rests on six groups, two of them contemporaneous.
weighing.overrides: Rank inversion check: no rejected value rests on a better class of writing than the default. Hodges's report (Seventeenth Georgia) prints 'until 3 p. m.' for the hour the march was resumed (the first text layer reads '3 i). m.'); it is ambiguous and is not used.

source_panel_text: About 05:00 (sunrise to 05:30): a British officer's diary of the day has Hood with Lee, Hill and Longstreet on the ridge at 5 a.m., and a regiment of his division reports leaving its bivouac at 3 a.m. for a march of about 3 miles. The plan's 06:30 has no source; 07:30 is when the whole column could be up. Five other values are listed.

what_would_change_it: A report, diary or letter of 2 July 1863 or of the weeks after it that gives the hour at which the first or the last brigade of Hood's division reached Seminary Ridge (the reports of Robertson's or Anderson's brigades if they exist, or a diary of the Texas or Georgia brigades), or the hour at which the Second Georgia halted 'after proceeding some 3 miles'; or the page image of Shepherd's report showing an hour other than 3 a.m.
owner_note: The first delegated default (06:30, a marked stand-in) is replaced by an inferred value; nothing is deleted and 06:30 stays selectable. The floor of the arrival gate would move from 05:30 to 05:00, which a diary of the day documents for Hood himself; the memoir value (sunrise) is a scenario, not the floor. How the floor is reconciled is recorded by the integration step, in the open.
